chief_complaint: wrist pain and tingling in her fingers
hpi_details: gradual onset of numbness, tingling, and burning pain in her right hand over the past two months. Affects the thumb, index, and middle fingers. Worse at night, often waking her up, and during long typing sessions at work. Eased by shaking her hand ('flick sign'). No pain in the neck, elbow, or shoulder. Normal grip strength and dexterity.
ideas: thinks it is related to computer work, keyboard ergonomics, or a pinched nerve in the wrist
concerns: worried she might need surgery or that the numbness will become permanent, which would affect her career
expectations: wants advice on wrist splints, ergonomics, or non-surgical treatments
social_hx: works as a software developer, spends 8-10 hours typing daily, non-smoker, plays tennis on weekends

clinical_knowledge.topic: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Recommend neutral-angle wrist splint to wear at night and during long typing sessions, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: wrist pain and tingling in her fingers

Key HPI features: gradual onset of numbness, tingling, and burning pain in her right hand over the past two months. Affects the thumb, index, and middle fingers. Worse at night, often waking her up, and during long typing sessions at work. Eased by shaking her hand ('flick sign'). No pain in the neck, elbow, or shoulder. Normal grip strength and dexterity.
Objective/Exam findings: Needs hand inspection (thenar atrophy check), sensory testing (median vs ulnar), motor strength (thumb abduction), Phalen's test, and Tinel's sign.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cervical radiculopathy (C6) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Constant numbness or thenar (thumb base) muscle wasting — signals more advanced nerve damage needing urgent referral.
management_principles: Recommend neutral-angle wrist splint to wear at night and during long typing sessions
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 29F software developer presents with 2-month history of right-hand numbness, tingling, and paresthesia in median nerve distribution (thumb, index, middle fingers). Worse at night and with keyboard use. Positive flick sign. No proximal symptoms, no motor weakness.
reference_soap.objective: Needs hand inspection (thenar atrophy check), sensory testing (median vs ulnar), motor strength (thumb abduction), Phalen's test, and Tinel's sign.
reference_soap.assessment: Mild to moderate Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS), right side. DDx: cervical radiculopathy (C6), pronator teres syndrome, de Quervain's tenosynovitis, diabetic neuropathy.
reference_soap.plan: Recommend neutral-angle wrist splint to wear at night and during long typing sessions. Counsel on ergonomic keyboard/mouse adjustments. Discuss short course of NSAIDs. Educate on signs of progression (thenar weakness, constant numbness) that warrant EMG/NCS or surgical referral.

learning_objectives: Elicit symptoms in the classic median nerve distribution
Identify aggravating factors (wrist flexion, typing, sleep positions) and relieving maneuvers (shaking hand)
Explain conservative management options (night splinting, ergonomics) clearly to the patient
Screen for motor deficits (weakness, wasting) and explain when to seek specialist review

teaching.one_liner: Compression of the median nerve at the wrist causes numbness and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers — classically worse at night and relieved by shaking the hand ('flick sign') — usually managed conservatively with a wrist splint first.
red_flags: Constant numbness or thenar (thumb base) muscle wasting — signals more advanced nerve damage needing urgent referral

must_ask.say: Which fingers are affected — your thumb, index, and middle finger?
Does this wake you up at night?
Does shaking your hand make it feel better?
Do you do a lot of typing or repetitive hand work?
Have you noticed any weakness in your grip or dropping things?

history.answer: My right wrist has been aching and the fingers on my right hand keep tingling.
It feels like tingling, numbness, and sometimes a burning sensation. I haven't noticed any actual muscle weakness in my hand.
It is only in my right hand, mostly my thumb, index, and middle fingers. My pinky finger feels completely normal.
It started gradually about two months ago. Before that, my hands felt completely fine.
It has been slowly getting worse and happening more often over the past two months.
Yes, it gets much worse at night and frequently wakes me up with burning and tingling in my hand.
When it wakes me up or flares up, shaking my hand back and forth vigorously helps relieve the tingling.
Typing on my computer keyboard during long days at work definitely makes the pain and tingling worse.
I can still button my shirts and I haven't been dropping cups or keys, though the numbness is very annoying.
No, I don't have any pain in my neck, shoulder, or elbow at all.
No, my speech has been fine, my face hasn't drooped, and I haven't had any vision changes or dizziness.
No, my bladder and bowel habits are completely normal, and I don't have any numbness between my legs.
No shortness of breath, no drooping eyelids, and no trouble chewing or swallowing food.
No, I haven't noticed any muscle twitches, and the palm of my hand doesn't look shrunken or thinner.
No, I haven't had any fever, cold, or diarrhea recently.
No, I don't have high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or any heart conditions.
I eat a regular balanced diet with meat and vegetables, and I've never had stomach surgery.
No, I am not taking steroids, chemotherapy, water pills, or any nerve medications.
I type eight to ten hours a day for work and play tennis on weekends, but I don't lean heavily on my elbows.
I only take over-the-counter ibuprofen once in a while when the wrist aches, which helps a little bit.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions and have always been healthy.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I don't have any allergies to medications or foods.
I don't smoke and have never smoked or vaped.
I only drink a glass of wine or beer socially once or twice a month.
I work full-time as a software developer and live in an apartment with my partner.
No one in my family has nerve problems, stroke, or autoimmune diseases.
My last menstrual period was two weeks ago, my cycles are regular, and there is no chance of pregnancy.
I think it might be from all the typing at work, maybe a pinched nerve in my wrist.
I am worried that this might need surgery or that permanent nerve damage could hurt my career as a developer.
I would like to know if wrist splints, changing my desk ergonomics, or other non-surgical options could fix this.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72/min regular, respiratory rate 14/min, temperature 36.6 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, comfortable young female in no acute distress, occasionally rubbing or shaking her right hand.
Facial symmetry intact, extraocular movements full without nystagmus, speech fluent without dysarthria.
Full active range of motion of cervical spine without tenderness; Spurling test is negative bilaterally.
Positive Phalen test producing tingling in the right thumb, index, and middle fingers within 30 seconds; positive Tinel sign at the right volar wrist; negative Finkelstein test.
Normal bulk and tone without thenar muscle atrophy; right thumb abduction (abductor pollicis brevis) and grip strength are 5/5 bilaterally.
Decreased pinprick and light touch sensation over the palmar aspect of the right thumb, index, middle finger, and radial half of the ring finger; sensation on the fifth finger is intact.
Biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric; Babinski sign is absent bilaterally.
Finger-to-nose coordination is normal bilaterally; gait is steady with normal arm swing and negative Romberg sign.
